extraction_notes.note: Equations (1.3)/(2.1), (2.3)/(4.1), (2.4)/(4.5), (2.5)/(4.10) are verbatim restatements; one node per repeated statement was applied to these numbered equations, keeping the Section 2 copy and adding hand edges for refs to the dropped labels 4.5 and 4.10 and to the Section 4 assumption nodes that contain the dropped copies.

The derivation of the optimal control, optimal state and NCE equation in Section 3.1 is a chain of unnamed 'we can rewrite ... as' steps in running text; each was emitted as a claim wrapping its numbered equations rather than as remarks or proof text.

Cited representations (optimal control via BSVIE from Shi-Wang-Yong/Yong; delay-to-Volterra transformation from Lindquist/Oksendal-Zhang) are stated in full in prose, so emitted as external theorems; they could also be read as applied citations.
Lemma 3.1 is presented without proof as 'easy to check'; treated as a standard uncited Fredholm solvability result (origin external) rather than a paper contribution.

Each special-case decentralized control is defined in one sentence that also introduces the closed-loop state and runs into the following theorem ('then we get the following asymptotic equilibrium analysis'); the whole sentence was kept.
Research directions in the concluding section (Volterra kernels in the cost, time inconsistency, delay-dependent consistency conditions) are informal outlook, not stated open problems.

nodes.statement:

nodes.statement: \widehat{c}(s,t)=c(s,t)+\int_{t}^{s}P(s,r)c(r,t)dr,\quad s\geq t.

nodes.statement: x_{i}(t)=\widehat{\varphi }(t)+\widehat{\sigma }_i(t)+\int_0^t\widehat{f}(t,s)a(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)u_{i}(s)ds,

\widehat{f}(t,s)&=f(t,s)+\int_{s}^{t}P(t,r)f(r,s)dr.

nodes.statement:

t,s\in[0,T].

nodes.name: Remarks on the optimal control, optimal state and NCE equation
nodes.statement:
Before concluding this section, let us make some remarks on
(\ref{3.6}), (\ref{3.9}) and (\ref{3.14}). Firstly, note that $\overline{u}_i(t)$ depends on the path of $\overline{x}_i$ in
$[t,T]$. Moreover, $\widehat{c}$ is a general non-separable function
of $(t,s)$. In particular, such a general feature can naturally
degenerate and transform into the form with Riccati equation
involved, see Section 4.1 below. Secondly, equation (\ref{3.9}) is a
new type of stochastic equation with double integrals, which is
essentially different from the corresponding equation in stochastic differential equations (SDEs) case.
Since it has both the characters of Volterra and Fredholm equation,
we then call it a stochastic Volterra-Fredholm equation. We will
study its solvability under certain conditions in next section by noting our main concern here is NCE equation. Thirdly, we express the NCE
equation in our setting by means of deterministic Volterra-Fredholm
equation. This idea is also different to other literature on SDEs.
nodes.statement_short: The optimal control depends on the future path; (3.9) is a new stochastic Volterra-Fredholm equation; the NCE equation is a deterministic Volterra-Fredholm equation.

$1\leq i\leq N,$ $\mathcal{J}_i(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})\leq
\mathcal{J}_i(u_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})+\epsilon, $ where $\epsilon>0$,
$\widehat{u}_{-i}=(\widehat{u}_1,\cdots,\widehat{u}_{i-1},\widehat{u}_{i+1},\cdots,\widehat{u}_{N})$,
$u_i\in L^2_{\mathcal{F}}(0,T;\mathbb{R})$, then we call this set of
controls $\widehat{u}_i$, $1\leq i\leq N$ an $\epsilon$-Nash
equilibrium with respect to costs $\mathcal{J}_i$ with $1\leq i\leq
N$.
nodes.statement_short: No player can lower its cost by more than $\epsilon$ by deviating unilaterally.

Comparing (\ref{3.19}) and (\ref{3.20}), we can rewrite $x_i(t)$ as

\begin{align*}
x_i(t)=& \; \overline{x}_i(t)+\int_0^t\widehat{f}(t,s)\Big[x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)\Big]ds \\
&-\frac{1}{R}\int_0^T\int_0^{s\wedge t}\widehat{c}(t,r)\widehat{c}(s,r)\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_r}[x_i(s)-\overline{x}_i(s)]drds.
\end{align*}

Therefore,

\begin{align*}
x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)=& \; \overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)+\int_0^t\widehat{f}(t,s)\Big[x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)\Big]ds\nonumber\\
& - \frac 1 R \int_0^T\int_0^{s\wedge
t}\widehat{c}(t,r)\widehat{c}(s,r)\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_r}[x^N(s)-\widehat{a}(s)]drds\nonumber\\
&+\frac 1 R \int_0^T\int_0^{s\wedge t}\widehat{c}(t,r)\widehat{c}(s,r)\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_r}[\overline{x}^N(s)-\widehat{a}(s)]drds.
\end{align*}

By using Lemma \ref{lemma6-1}, Lemma \ref{lemma-2}, together with
the boundedness of $\widehat{f}$ and $\widehat{c}$, we can obtain
the desired result (\ref{3.23}).
\hfill
nodes.statement_short: Write the difference equations for $x_i-\overline x_i$ and $x^N-\widehat a$, then apply Lemmas 3.2 and 3.3.

nodes.name: Theorem 3.3 (cost approximation)
nodes.statement:
Suppose $\varphi$, $f$, $b$ and $c$ are bounded and continuous in
$t$, NCE equation (\ref{3.14}) admits a unique continuous solution
$\widehat{a}\in C[0,T]$, $\overline{u}_i$ is the optimal control
with state equation (\ref{3.1}), cost functional (\ref{3.2}) that is
parameterized by $\widehat{a}$, (\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for two
cases of $A=\widehat{f}$, $B=\widehat{c},$ and $A=0,$
$B=\widehat{c}$. Then for $1\leq i\leq N$, we have
\begin{eqnarray}
\mid\mathcal{J}_i(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})-\overline{J}_i(\overline{u}_i)\mid=O\left(\frac
{1} {\sqrt{N}}\right).
\end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: The cost of agent $i$ under decentralized controls is within $O(1/\sqrt N)$ of its limiting optimal cost.
assumptions:
Suppose $\varphi$, $f$, $b$ and $c$ are bounded and continuous in
$t$
NCE equation (\ref{3.14}) admits a unique continuous solution

(\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for two
cases
conclusions:
\mid\mathcal{J}_i(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})-\overline{J}_i(\overline{u}_i)\mid=O\left(\frac
{1} {\sqrt{N}}\right).
nodes.label: theorem3.2

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.3
nodes.statement_short: Expand the cost difference, bound control and state gaps by Schwarz's inequality, and conclude with Lemma 3.4.

nodes.name: Perturbation sizes epsilon_a and epsilon_b
nodes.statement:
In the following part, given two processes $\xi _{a}$, $\xi _{b}$ in $L^2_{\mathcal{F}}(0,T;\mathbb{R})$, we denote by
 
\begin{eqnarray} \epsilon _{a}=\left( \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\xi _{a}(t)|^{2}dt\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}<\infty , \quad
\epsilon _{b}=\left( \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\xi _{b}(t)|^{2}dt\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}<\infty .
\end{eqnarray}

nodes.name: Perturbed control problem
nodes.statement:
For
comparison, we also discuss one perturbed version with state
equation

\begin{align}
x_{i}(t) = & \;\varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)x_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)
\widehat{a}(s)ds \nonumber \\
&+\int_{0}^{t}g(t,s)\xi
_{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma
(t,s)dW_{i}(s), \end{align}

and the cost functional
\[
J_{i}^{\xi }(u_{i})=\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left[ |x_{i}(t)-\gamma
\widehat{a}(t)-\eta +\xi _{b}(t)|^{2}+R|u_{i}(t)|^{2}\right]dt.
\]
Here $g$ is bounded deterministic function.
nodes.statement_short: The limiting control problem with additive perturbations $\xi_a$ in the state and $\xi_b$ in the cost.

nodes.name: Lemma 3.5 (cost lower bound under perturbation)
nodes.statement:
Suppose $\overline{u}_{i}$ is an optimal control given in
(\ref{3.6}) and
\begin{eqnarray} \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)|^{2}dt+\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|u_{i}(t)|^{2}dt\leq
C_{0}.
\end{eqnarray}

where $ x_{i},$ $u_{i}$ are defined in (\ref{6.7}), $C_{0}$ is a
fixed constant. Moreover, $\widehat{a}$ is continuous and bounded,
(\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c},$ then we
have

\[
J_{i}^{\xi }(u_{i})\geq
\overline{J}_{i}(\overline{u}_{i})-C(1+\epsilon_b)(\epsilon_a+\epsilon_b).
\]
nodes.statement_short: Perturbations of size $\epsilon_a,\epsilon_b$ can lower the optimal cost by at most $C(1+\epsilon_b)(\epsilon_a+\epsilon_b)$.
assumptions:
Suppose $\overline{u}_{i}$ is an optimal control given in
(\ref{3.6})
Moreover, $\widehat{a}$ is continuous and bounded,
(\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c},$
conclusions:
J_{i}^{\xi }(u_{i})\geq
\overline{J}_{i}(\overline{u}_{i})-C(1+\epsilon_b)(\epsilon_a+\epsilon_b).
nodes.label: lemma6.2

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.5
nodes.statement:
For convenience, we can rewrite (\ref{6.7}) as
 
\begin{align*}
x_{i}(t) = & \; \varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)x_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}^{\prime }(s)ds \\
&+\int_{0}^{t}g(t,s)\xi _{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)\overline{u}_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma (t,s)dW_{i}(s).
\end{align*}

Here $u_{i}^{\prime }(s)=u_{i}(s)-\overline{u}_{i}(s),$

\[
\overline{u}_{i}(s)=-\frac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}
(r,t)[x_{i}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]dr,
\]
where $x_{i}$ satisfies (\ref{6.7}), $\widehat{c}$ is given in
(\ref{3.7}). It then follows from inequality (\ref{6.8}) that
$\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|u_{i}^{\prime }(t)|^{2}dt\leq C$. Next we
construct one auxiliary optimal control problem with state equation
and cost functional as

\begin{align}
\widetilde{x}_{i}(t) = & \; \varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)\widetilde{x}_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds \nonumber \\
&+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}''(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)\overline{u}_{i}(s,\widetilde{x}_{i})ds+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma (t,s)dW_{i}(s), \end{align}

and

\[
\widetilde{J}_{i}(u_{i}'')=\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left[|\widetilde{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma \widehat{a}(t)-\eta |^{2}+R|u_{i}''(t)+\overline{u}_{i}(t,\widetilde{x}_{i})|^{2}\right]dt.
\]

where $u''_{i}$ is the control variable. For $t\in[0,T]$,
$\overline{u}_{i}(t,\widetilde{x}_{i})$ in (\ref{6.9}) is defined as

\[
\overline{u}_{i}(t,\widetilde{x}_{i})=-\frac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\!\!\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)[\widetilde{x}_{i}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]dr.
\]

Obviously, $\widetilde{J}_{i}(u_{i}'')$ attains its
minimum when $u_{i}''=0,$ and the corresponding cost functional equals to $
\overline{J}_{i}(\overline{u}_{i}).$ On the other hand, by Lemma \ref{lemma6-1},
\[
M_{i}'(t)=\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}'(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)M_{i}'(s)ds-\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)M_{i}'(r)drds
\]

admits a unique solution $M_{i}'$ such that

\[
\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|M_{i}^{\prime }(t)|^{2}dt\leq 6\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}'(s)ds\right\vert^{2}dt\leq C.
\]

If we take $u_{i}''=u_{i}'(s)=u_{i}(s)-\overline{u}_{i}(s)$, and
$\widetilde{x}_{i}'$ is the corresponding solution of (\ref{6.9}), then $\widetilde{x}_{i}'=\overline{x}_{i}(t)+M_{i}'(t),$ where $\overline{x}_{i}(t)$ is the
optimal state in (\ref{3.9}) with $a=\widehat{a}$. Moreover,
recalling the boundedness of $\overline{x}_i$ in
$L^2_{\mathcal{F}}(0,T;\mathbb{R})$, we also have
$\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widetilde{x}_{i}'(t)|^{2}dt\leq C$.
Since $x_{i}$ and $\widetilde{x}_{i}'$ are given in
(\ref{6.7}) and (\ref{6.9}), thus their difference
$d_{i}=x_{i}-\widetilde{x}_{i}'$ satisfy

\[
d_{i}(t)=\int_{0}^{t}g(t,s)\xi _{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)d_{i}(s)ds-\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\!\!\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)d_{i}(r)drds.
\]

Under above requirements, from Lemma \ref{lemma6-1}, we have

\[
\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)-\widetilde{x}_{i}^{\prime }(t)|^{2}dt\leq 6\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert\int_{0}^{t}g(t,s)\xi _{a}(s)ds\right\vert^{2}dt\leq C\epsilon _{a}^{2}.
\]

Following the similar arguments in \cite{N-H 2012}, we should have

\[
|J_{i}^{\xi}(u_{i})-\widetilde{J}_{i}(u_{i}')| \leq
C(1+\epsilon_b)(\epsilon _{a}+\epsilon _{b}),
\]

where $C$ does not depend on $\xi_a$ and $\xi_b$. After combining the
estimate of $\widetilde{J}_{i}(u_{i}')\geq
\overline{J}_i(\overline{u}_i)$, we can get the desired result.
\hfill
nodes.statement_short: Compare with an auxiliary control problem whose minimum equals the limiting optimal cost; Lemma 3.2 controls the state differences.

nodes.name: Lemma 3.6 (uniform boundedness of costs)
nodes.statement:
Suppose $\widehat{a}$ is solution of NCE equation (\ref{3.14}),
(\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for two cases of $A=\widehat{f}$,
$B=\widehat{c}$, and $A=0$, $B=\widehat{c}$. Then
$\mathcal{J}_{i}(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})\leq C$, where $C$
does not depend on $N$.
nodes.statement_short: Under decentralized controls each agent's cost is bounded uniformly in $N$.
assumptions: Suppose $\widehat{a}$ is solution of NCE equation (\ref{3.14}),

(\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for two cases of $A=\widehat{f}$,
$B=\widehat{c}$, and $A=0$, $B=\widehat{c}$.
conclusions:
$\mathcal{J}_{i}(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})\leq C$, where $C$
does not depend on $N$.
nodes.label: lemma6.3

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.6
nodes.statement:
If we can prove

\[
\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(s)|^{2}ds\leq C,\quad
\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(s)|^{2}ds\leq C,
\]

where $x_i$ satisfies (\ref{3.19}), $C$ does not depend on $N,$ then
the result holds directly. From (\ref{3.19}), we have

\begin{align}
x^{N}(t) = & \; \widehat{\varphi }(t)+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)x^{N}(s)ds+\frac{1}{N}\sum_{l=1}^{N}\widehat{\sigma }_{l}(t) \nonumber \\
&-\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)\frac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}s}\int_{s}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,s)[x^{N}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]drds, \end{align}

where $x^{N}(t)=\frac{1}{N}\sum\limits_{l=1}^{N}x_{l}(t).$ Note that
(\ref{6.10}) is one special case of equation (\ref{6.1}),
(\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for $A=\widehat{f}$,
$B=\widehat{c}$, it then follows from Lemma \ref{lemma6-1} that

\begin{align}
\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x^{N}(s)|^{2}ds \leq & \; C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{\varphi}(s)|^{2}ds+C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert \frac{1}{N}\sum_{l=1}^{N}\widehat{\sigma}_{l}(t)\right\vert ^{2}dt \nonumber \\
& +C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{a}(s)|^{2}ds+C. \end{align}

As to $x_i$ in equation (\ref{3.19}), using (\ref{6.11}) and
conditions (\ref{6.2}), (\ref{6.3}) with $A=0$, $B=\widehat{c}$, we
should have $\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(s)|^{2}ds\leq C$ where $C$ is
independent of $N$. At last, we know that

\begin{align*}
\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt
= & \; \frac{1}{R^{2}}\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)[x_{i}(r)-\gamma\widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]dr\right\vert ^{2}dt \\
\leq & \; \frac{1}{R^{2}}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{t}^{T}|\widehat{c}(r,t)|^{2}drdt\cdot \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}[x_{i}(r)-\gamma\widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]^{2}dr.
\end{align*}

Hence $\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt$ is bounded, too.
Then the desired result holds.
\hfill
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to $L^2$ bounds on state and control; bound the state average by Lemma 3.2, then each state and control.

nodes.name: Lemma 3.7 (mean field approximation under unilateral deviation)
nodes.statement:
Suppose $\widehat{a}$ is the solution of NCE equation (\ref{3.14}),
(\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for two cases of $A=\widehat{f}$,
$B=\widehat{c}$ and $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c}$. Moreover,
$(1+K_2)K_1\frac{360}{N^{2}R^2}L^2<\frac 1 2$, where

\[
L=\int_0^T\int_0^t|\widehat{c}(t,s)|^2dsdt, \quad
K_1=\int_0^T\int_0^t|\widehat{f}(t,s)|^2dsdt,\quad
K_2=\int_0^T\int_0^t|P_0(t,s)|^2dsdt,
\]
$P_0$ is defined in (\ref{6.3}) with $A=\widehat{f}$. Then we have

\begin{eqnarray*}
\mathbb{E}\int_0^T|\widehat{a}(s)-x^{N}(s)|^2ds=O\Big(\frac{1}{N}\Big),
\end{eqnarray*}

where $x^{N}(t)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{l=1}^{N}x_{l}(t),$ $x_l$
satisfies (\ref{6.12}) and (\ref{6.13}).
nodes.statement_short: If one agent deviates while others use decentralized controls, the state average stays $O(1/N)$-close to $\widehat a$.
assumptions: Suppose $\widehat{a}$ is the solution of NCE equation (\ref{3.14}),

Moreover,
$(1+K_2)K_1\frac{360}{N^{2}R^2}L^2<\frac 1 2$
conclusions: \mathbb{E}\int_0^T|\widehat{a}(s)-x^{N}(s)|^2ds=O\Big(\frac{1}{N}\Big),
nodes.label: lemma6.4

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.7
nodes.statement:
For convenience, we also rewrite (\ref{6.13}) as

\begin{align}
x_{i}(t) = & \; \varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)x_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)\widehat{u}_{i}(s)ds \nonumber \\
& +\int_{0}^{t}\sigma (t,s)dW_{i}(s)+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)[x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)]ds \nonumber \\
& +\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)[u_{i}(s)-\widehat{u}_{i}(s)]ds, \end{align}

where $\widehat{u}_i$ is defined as
\begin{eqnarray} \widehat{u}_{i}(t)=-\frac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\!\!\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)[x_{i}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]dr,
\end{eqnarray}

and $x_{i}$ satisfies (\ref{6.13}). After some direct calculations,

\begin{align*}
x^{N}(t) = & \; \widehat{\varphi }(t)+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds+\frac{1}{N}\sum_{l=1}^{N}\widehat{\sigma }_{l}(t) \\
& -\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)\frac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}s}\int_{s}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,s)[x^{N}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]drds \\
& +\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)[x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)]ds+\frac{1}{N}\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)[u_{i}(s)-\widehat{u}_{i}(s)]ds,
\end{align*}

where $\widehat{\varphi}$, $\widehat{f}$, $\widehat{\sigma}_l$ are
defined in (\ref{3.8.1}). Using Fubini theorem, it also follows from
(\ref{3.9}) (with $a=\widehat{a}$) that

\begin{align*}
\overline{x}^{N}(t) = & \; \widehat{\varphi }(t)+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds+\frac{1}{N}\sum_{l=1}^{N}\widehat{\sigma }_{l}(t) \\
&
-\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)\frac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}s}\!\!\int_{s}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,s)[\overline{x}^{N}(r)-\gamma
\widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]drds,
\end{align*}

therefore we have

\begin{align}
x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t) = & \; \overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)[x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)]ds \nonumber \\
& -\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)\frac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}s}\!\!\int_{s}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,s)[x^{N}(r)-\widehat{a}(r)]drds \nonumber \\
& +\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)\frac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}s}\!\!\int_{s}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,s)[\overline{x}^{N}(r)-\widehat{a}(r)]drds \nonumber \\
& +\frac{1}{N}\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)[u_{i}(s)-\widehat{u}_{i}(s)]ds. \end{align}

Note that if $A=0$, $B=\widehat{c}$, then (\ref{6.2}) and
(\ref{6.3}) imply $\overline{x}^N$ is bounded in
$L^2_{\mathcal{F}}(0,T;\mathbb{R}).$ Similarly, if (\ref{6.2}) and
(\ref{6.3}) hold with  $A=\widehat{f}$, $B=\widehat{c}$, then using
Lemma \ref{lemma6-1} to (\ref{6.16}), we have

\begin{eqnarray} &&\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt \nonumber\\ &&\leq
(1+K_2)\left[(36+12R^2)\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt+\frac{36}{N^{2}}L\cdot
\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}[u_{i}(s)-\widehat{u}_{i}(s)]^{2}ds\right],
\end{eqnarray}

where $L$ and $K_2$ are defined before.

On the other hand, from Lemma \ref{lemma6.3},
$\mathcal{J}_i(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})$ is bounded, it then
suffices to consider $u_i$ in (\ref{6.13}) such that
$\mathcal{J}_i(u_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})\leq
\mathcal{J}_i(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})$, which implies that
$\mathbb{E}\int_0^T|u_i(t)|^2dt\leq C$.  As to $\widehat{u}_i$ in
(\ref{6.15}), we have

\begin{align*}
\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt = & \; \frac{1}{R^{2}}\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)[x_{i}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]dr\right\vert ^{2}dt \\
\leq & \; \frac{1}{R^{2}}L\cdot \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}[x_{i}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]^{2}dr,
\end{align*}

therefore,

\begin{align}
\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}[u_{i}(s)-\widehat{u}_{i}(s)]^{2}ds
\leq & \; 2\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|u_{i}(s)|^{2}ds+2\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(s)|^{2}ds \nonumber \\
\leq & \; C+\frac{2}{R^{2}}L\cdot \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(r)|^{2}dr, \end{align}

where $C$ does not depend on $N$. Substituting (\ref{6.18}) into
(\ref{6.17}), we have

\begin{eqnarray} &&\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt\nonumber\\
&& \leq
(1+K_2)(36+12R^2)\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt\nonumber
\\
&&+\frac{C}{N^{2}}+ (1+K_2)\frac{72}{N^{2}R^2}L^2\cdot
\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}[u_{i}(s)-\widehat{u}_{i}(s)]^{2}ds.
\end{eqnarray}

After some transformations, we can rewrite (\ref{6.13}) as

\begin{align*}
x_{i}(t) = & \; \widehat{\varphi }(t)+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)[x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)]ds \\
& +\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)u_{i}(s)ds+\widehat{\sigma }_{i}(t),
\end{align*}

therefore,

\begin{align}
\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)|^{2}dt
\leq & \; 5\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{\varphi }(t)|^{2}dt+5\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{t}|\widehat{f}(t,s)|^{2}dsdt\cdot\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)|^{2}ds \nonumber \\
& +5\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{t}|\widehat{f}(t,s)|^2dsdt\cdot \int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{a}(s)|^{2}ds \nonumber \\
& +5\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{t}|\widehat{c}(t,s)|^{2}dsdt\cdot\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|u_{i}(s)|^{2}ds+\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{\sigma}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt. \end{align}

Since $\widehat{\varphi}$, $\widehat{f}$, $\widehat{a}$, $\sigma$
are bounded, substituting (\ref{6.19}) into (\ref{6.20}) yields
\begin{eqnarray*}
\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)|^{2}dt\leq C+C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{
x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt+
(1+K_2)K_1\frac{360}{N^{2}R^2}L^2\cdot
\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}[x_{i}(s)]^{2}ds.
\end{eqnarray*}

So if $(1+K_2)K_1\frac{360}{N^{2}R^2}L^2<\frac 1 2,$ then we have
\[
\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)|^{2}dt\leq C+C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{x}^{N}(t)-
\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt,
\]
which implies the boundedness of $\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)|^{2}dt$.
By combining (\ref{6.19}), (\ref{6.20}) and Lemma \ref{lemma-2}, we obtained the desired result.
\hfill
nodes.statement_short: Derive the equation for $x^N-\widehat a$, bound it by Lemma 3.2 in terms of the deviation, then absorb the deviating state's norm. The key step is the absorption under the condition $(1+K_2)K_1\frac{360}{N^2R^2}L^2<\frac12$.

nodes.name: Remark on the generality of Lemma 3.7
nodes.statement:
Compared with Lemma 3.4 above, our result here seems to be more
general because $u_i$ in (\ref{6.13}) is not necessary to be
$\widehat{u}_i$ in (\ref{3.18}). Moreover, our result also
generalizes the corresponding result in \cite{N-H 2012} in
that our state equation can degenerate to the linear SDEs there.
In addition, our approach here is also different from the
one used in \cite{N-H 2012}. At last, although the conditions imposed on above coefficients $K_1$, $K_2$ and $L$ seem to be technical, it
has two interesting features. First, the above inequality holds true in general because $N$ is always sufficiently large. Second,
such condition is not required in the nontrivial case $\widehat{f}=0.$

nodes.name: Theorem 3.4 (epsilon-Nash equilibrium of decentralized controls)
nodes.statement:

solution $\widehat{a}\in C[0,T]$. (\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold
with $A=\widehat{f}$, $B=\widehat{c}$ and $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c}$.
Moreover, $(1+K_2)K_1\frac{360}{N^{2}R^2}L^2<\frac 1 2$, where $L,\
K_1,\ K_2$ are defined in Lemma \ref{lemma6.4}. Then the set of
control $\widehat{u}_i$ in (\ref{3.18}) with $1\leq i\leq N$ for $N$
players is an $\epsilon$-Nash equilibrium, i.e., for $1\leq i\leq
N$,
$$\mathcal{J}_i(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})-\epsilon\leq
\inf\limits_{u_i\in
L^2_{\mathcal{F}}[0,T]}\mathcal{J}_i(u_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})\leq
\mathcal{J}_i(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i}).
$$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.4
nodes.statement:
If we denote by $\xi_a(t)=x^N(t)-\widehat{a}(t),$
$\xi_b(t)=\gamma(\widehat{a}(t)-x^N(t))$, then the dynamics and cost functional
of $\mathcal{A}_i$ can be rewritten as

\begin{align}
x_{i}(t) = & \; \varphi(t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)x_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds \nonumber \\
& +\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)\xi_{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma(t,s)dW_{i}(s), \end{align}

and

\[
J_{i}(u_{i})=\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left[ |x_{i}(t)-\gamma\widehat{a}(t)-\eta +\xi _{b}(t)|^{2}+R|u_{i}(t)|^{2}\right]dt.
\]

From Lemma \ref{lemma6.4}, we have
$\epsilon_a+\epsilon_b=O(\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}})$, and
$\mathbb{E}\int_0^T|x_i(t)|^2dt+\mathbb{E}\int_0^T|u_i(t)|^2dt\leq C,$ where $C$
is independent of $N$, $\epsilon_a$, $\epsilon_b$ are defined in
(\ref{6.6}), it then follows from Lemma \ref{lemma6.4}, Theorem
\ref{theorem3.2} that

\[
\mathcal{J}_i(u_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})\geq \overline{J}_i(\overline{u}_i)-O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}\right) \geq \mathcal{J}_i(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})-O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}\right).
\]

The conclusion is thus proved.
\hfill

which can fill this technical gap.

nodes.name: Freeze and solve Volterra equation
nodes.statement:
Given $y(\cdot )\in L_{\mathcal{F}}^{2}(0,T;\mathbb{R}),$ consider the
following Volterra equation
\begin{eqnarray} x(t)=\varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}A(t,s)x(s)ds-\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{s
\wedge t}B(t,r)B(s,r)\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{r}}y(s)drds,
\end{eqnarray}

which obviously admits a unique solution $x(\cdot)$ under above
assumptions.
nodes.statement_short: Freeze the Fredholm term at $y$ and solve the resulting Volterra equation.

nodes.name: Resolvent rewriting
nodes.statement:
By using Lemma 1.1 in
\cite{Y 1996}, we can rewrite (\ref{6.5}) as

\[
x(t)=\widehat{\varphi }(t)-\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{s\wedge t}
\widehat{B}(t,r)B(s,r)\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{r}}y(s)drds.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite via the resolvent kernel (Pritchard-You Lemma 1.1).

nodes.name: Contraction argument
nodes.statement:
Then using the idea of contraction mapping and Lemma \ref{lemma-1},
together with above requirements, we can obtain the existence of
$x(\cdot)$ in $L_{\mathcal{F}}^{2}(0,T;\mathbb{R})$ satisfying
(\ref{6.4}).
nodes.statement_short: Contraction mapping with Lemma 3.1 gives existence and the bound (6.4).

nodes.name: Reduce to (6.1)
nodes.statement:
From (\ref{3.14}) and (\ref{3.20}), we know the difference between
$\overline{x}_i$ and $\widehat{a}$ satisfies the type of Equation
(\ref{6.1}) with $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c}$,
$\varphi=\widehat{\sigma}_i$.
nodes.statement_short: The difference $\overline x_i-\widehat a$ solves an equation of type (6.1).

nodes.name: Apply (6.4)
nodes.statement_short: Apply estimate (6.4) to the averaged difference.

nodes.name: Independence gives O(1/N)
nodes.statement:
It then follows from the boundedness of $\sigma$ and $P$ in
(\ref{3.8.1}), together with the independence of $W_i$
($i=1,2,\cdots,N$) that

\[
\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt=O\left(\frac{1}{N}\right),
\]

which implies the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Independence of the $W_i$ gives the $O(1/N)$ rate.

nodes.name: Rewrite x_i
nodes.statement_short: Express $x_i$ through $\overline x_i$ and the mean field error.

nodes.name: Equation for x^N - a-hat
nodes.statement:
Therefore,

\begin{align*}
x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)=& \; \overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)+\int_0^t\widehat{f}(t,s)\Big[x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)\Big]ds\nonumber\\
& - \frac 1 R \int_0^T\int_0^{s\wedge
t}\widehat{c}(t,r)\widehat{c}(s,r)\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_r}[x^N(s)-\widehat{a}(s)]drds\nonumber\\
&+\frac 1 R \int_0^T\int_0^{s\wedge t}\widehat{c}(t,r)\widehat{c}(s,r)\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_r}[\overline{x}^N(s)-\widehat{a}(s)]drds.
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Derive the equation for $x^N-\widehat a$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemmas 3.2, 3.3
nodes.statement:
By using Lemma \ref{lemma6-1}, Lemma \ref{lemma-2}, together with
the boundedness of $\widehat{f}$ and $\widehat{c}$, we can obtain
the desired result (\ref{3.23}).
nodes.statement_short: Lemmas 3.2 and 3.3 with bounded kernels give (3.23).

nodes.name: Expand cost difference
nodes.statement_short: Bound the cost difference by control and state gaps.

nodes.name: Control gap bound
nodes.statement:
It follows from (\ref{3.3}) and
(\ref{3.18}) that

\begin{align*}
\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)-\overline{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt
\leq & \; \frac{1}{R^{2}}\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\left\vert
\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(s,t)[x_{i}(s)-\overline{x}_{i}(s)]ds\right\vert ^{2}dt \\
\leq & \; C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(s)-\overline{x}_{i}(s)|^{2}ds.
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the control gap by the state gap.

nodes.name: Boundedness of optimal pair
nodes.statement:
Note that equation (\ref{3.20}) is one special case of (\ref{6.1})
with $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c}$. Under above requirement, then from
inequality (\ref{6.4}) above we have the boundedness of
$\overline{x}_i$ in $L^2_{\mathcal{F}}(0,T;\mathbb{R})$. Recalling
(\ref{3.6}) with $a=\widehat{a}$, we can also get similar
boundedness result for $\overline{u}_i$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3.2's estimate (6.4) bounds $\overline x_i$ and $\overline u_i$.

nodes.name: Schwarz on control term
nodes.statement_short: Schwarz's inequality on the cross term in the controls.

nodes.name: Split state term
nodes.statement_short: Split the state term into individual and mean field errors.

nodes.name: Schwarz on state term
nodes.statement_short: Schwarz's inequality on the state cross term.

nodes.name: Conclude via Lemma 3.4
nodes.statement: Therefore, by using Lemma \ref{lemma-3}, we obtain the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3.4 gives the $O(1/\sqrt N)$ rate.

nodes.name: Decompose the control
nodes.statement:
For convenience, we can rewrite (\ref{6.7}) as
 
\begin{align*}
x_{i}(t) = & \; \varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)x_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}^{\prime }(s)ds \\
&+\int_{0}^{t}g(t,s)\xi _{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)\overline{u}_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma (t,s)dW_{i}(s).
\end{align*}

Here $u_{i}^{\prime }(s)=u_{i}(s)-\overline{u}_{i}(s),$

\[
\overline{u}_{i}(s)=-\frac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}
(r,t)[x_{i}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]dr,
\]
where $x_{i}$ satisfies (\ref{6.7}), $\widehat{c}$ is given in
(\ref{3.7}).
nodes.statement_short: Write the control as $\overline u_i$ plus a deviation $u_i'$.

nodes.name: Bound deviation
nodes.statement:
It then follows from inequality (\ref{6.8}) that
$\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|u_{i}^{\prime }(t)|^{2}dt\leq C$.
nodes.statement_short: The deviation $u_i'$ is bounded in $L^2$.

nodes.name: Auxiliary problem
nodes.statement:
Next we
construct one auxiliary optimal control problem with state equation
and cost functional as

\begin{align}
\widetilde{x}_{i}(t) = & \; \varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)\widetilde{x}_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds \nonumber \\
&+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}''(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)\overline{u}_{i}(s,\widetilde{x}_{i})ds+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma (t,s)dW_{i}(s), \end{align}

and

\[
\widetilde{J}_{i}(u_{i}'')=\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left[|\widetilde{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma \widehat{a}(t)-\eta |^{2}+R|u_{i}''(t)+\overline{u}_{i}(t,\widetilde{x}_{i})|^{2}\right]dt.
\]

where $u''_{i}$ is the control variable. For $t\in[0,T]$,
$\overline{u}_{i}(t,\widetilde{x}_{i})$ in (\ref{6.9}) is defined as

\[
\overline{u}_{i}(t,\widetilde{x}_{i})=-\frac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\!\!\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)[\widetilde{x}_{i}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]dr.
\]

Obviously, $\widetilde{J}_{i}(u_{i}'')$ attains its
minimum when $u_{i}''=0,$ and the corresponding cost functional equals to $
\overline{J}_{i}(\overline{u}_{i}).$
nodes.statement_short: Introduce an auxiliary control problem minimized at $u''=0$ with value $\overline J_i(\overline u_i)$.

nodes.name: Solve deviation equation
nodes.statement:
On the other hand, by Lemma \ref{lemma6-1},
\[
M_{i}'(t)=\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}'(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)M_{i}'(s)ds-\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)M_{i}'(r)drds
\]

admits a unique solution $M_{i}'$ such that

\[
\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|M_{i}^{\prime }(t)|^{2}dt\leq 6\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}'(s)ds\right\vert^{2}dt\leq C.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3.2 solves the deviation equation for $M_i'$ with an $L^2$ bound.

nodes.name: Substitute deviation
nodes.statement:
If we take $u_{i}''=u_{i}'(s)=u_{i}(s)-\overline{u}_{i}(s)$, and
$\widetilde{x}_{i}'$ is the corresponding solution of (\ref{6.9}), then $\widetilde{x}_{i}'=\overline{x}_{i}(t)+M_{i}'(t),$ where $\overline{x}_{i}(t)$ is the
optimal state in (\ref{3.9}) with $a=\widehat{a}$. Moreover,
recalling the boundedness of $\overline{x}_i$ in
$L^2_{\mathcal{F}}(0,T;\mathbb{R})$, we also have
$\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widetilde{x}_{i}'(t)|^{2}dt\leq C$.
nodes.statement_short: Plug $u''=u'$ into the auxiliary problem; its state is $\overline x_i+M_i'$.

nodes.name: Difference equation
nodes.statement:
Since $x_{i}$ and $\widetilde{x}_{i}'$ are given in
(\ref{6.7}) and (\ref{6.9}), thus their difference
$d_{i}=x_{i}-\widetilde{x}_{i}'$ satisfy

\[
d_{i}(t)=\int_{0}^{t}g(t,s)\xi _{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)d_{i}(s)ds-\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\!\!\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)d_{i}(r)drds.
\]
nodes.statement_short: The state difference $d_i$ solves an equation of type (6.1).

nodes.name: Bound difference
nodes.statement:
Under above requirements, from Lemma \ref{lemma6-1}, we have

\[
\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)-\widetilde{x}_{i}^{\prime }(t)|^{2}dt\leq 6\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert\int_{0}^{t}g(t,s)\xi _{a}(s)ds\right\vert^{2}dt\leq C\epsilon _{a}^{2}.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3.2 bounds $d_i$ by $C\epsilon_a^2$.

nodes.name: Cost difference bound
nodes.statement:
Following the similar arguments in \cite{N-H 2012}, we should have

\[
|J_{i}^{\xi}(u_{i})-\widetilde{J}_{i}(u_{i}')| \leq
C(1+\epsilon_b)(\epsilon _{a}+\epsilon _{b}),
\]

where $C$ does not depend on $\xi_a$ and $\xi_b$.
nodes.statement_short: As in Nguyen-Huang, the cost difference is $C(1+\epsilon_b)(\epsilon_a+\epsilon_b)$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement:
After combining the
estimate of $\widetilde{J}_{i}(u_{i}')\geq
\overline{J}_i(\overline{u}_i)$, we can get the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Combine with optimality of the auxiliary problem.

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement:
If we can prove

\[
\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(s)|^{2}ds\leq C,\quad
\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(s)|^{2}ds\leq C,
\]

where $x_i$ satisfies (\ref{3.19}), $C$ does not depend on $N,$ then
the result holds directly.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to uniform $L^2$ bounds on $\widehat u_i$ and $x_i$.

nodes.name: Average equation
nodes.statement_short: Average the closed-loop equations to get (6.10).

nodes.name: Bound state average
nodes.statement:
Note that
(\ref{6.10}) is one special case of equation (\ref{6.1}),
(\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for $A=\widehat{f}$,
$B=\widehat{c}$, it then follows from Lemma \ref{lemma6-1} that

\begin{align}
\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x^{N}(s)|^{2}ds \leq & \; C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{\varphi}(s)|^{2}ds+C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert \frac{1}{N}\sum_{l=1}^{N}\widehat{\sigma}_{l}(t)\right\vert ^{2}dt \nonumber \\
& +C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{a}(s)|^{2}ds+C. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3.2 bounds the state average (6.11).

nodes.name: Bound individual state
nodes.statement:
As to $x_i$ in equation (\ref{3.19}), using (\ref{6.11}) and
conditions (\ref{6.2}), (\ref{6.3}) with $A=0$, $B=\widehat{c}$, we
should have $\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(s)|^{2}ds\leq C$ where $C$ is
independent of $N$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound each state uniformly in $N$.

nodes.name: Bound control and conclude
nodes.statement:
At last, we know that

\begin{align*}
\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt
= & \; \frac{1}{R^{2}}\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)[x_{i}(r)-\gamma\widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]dr\right\vert ^{2}dt \\
\leq & \; \frac{1}{R^{2}}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{t}^{T}|\widehat{c}(r,t)|^{2}drdt\cdot \mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}[x_{i}(r)-\gamma\widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]^{2}dr.
\end{align*}

Hence $\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt$ is bounded, too.
Then the desired result holds.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the control and conclude.

nodes.name: Rewrite deviating dynamics
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the deviating player's dynamics relative to $\widehat u_i$.

nodes.name: State average equation
nodes.statement:
After some direct calculations,

\begin{align*}
x^{N}(t) = & \; \widehat{\varphi }(t)+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds+\frac{1}{N}\sum_{l=1}^{N}\widehat{\sigma }_{l}(t) \\
& -\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)\frac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}s}\int_{s}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,s)[x^{N}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]drds \\
& +\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)[x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)]ds+\frac{1}{N}\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)[u_{i}(s)-\widehat{u}_{i}(s)]ds,
\end{align*}

where $\widehat{\varphi}$, $\widehat{f}$, $\widehat{\sigma}_l$ are
defined in (\ref{3.8.1}).
nodes.statement_short: Equation for the state average.

nodes.name: Difference equation (6.16)
nodes.statement:
Using Fubini theorem, it also follows from
(\ref{3.9}) (with $a=\widehat{a}$) that

\begin{align*}
\overline{x}^{N}(t) = & \; \widehat{\varphi }(t)+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds+\frac{1}{N}\sum_{l=1}^{N}\widehat{\sigma }_{l}(t) \\
&
-\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)\frac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}s}\!\!\int_{s}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,s)[\overline{x}^{N}(r)-\gamma
\widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]drds,
\end{align*}

therefore we have

\begin{align}
x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t) = & \; \overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)[x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)]ds \nonumber \\
& -\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)\frac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}s}\!\!\int_{s}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,s)[x^{N}(r)-\widehat{a}(r)]drds \nonumber \\
& +\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)\frac{1}{R}\mathbb{E}^{\mathcal{F}s}\!\!\int_{s}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,s)[\overline{x}^{N}(r)-\widehat{a}(r)]drds \nonumber \\
& +\frac{1}{N}\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)[u_{i}(s)-\widehat{u}_{i}(s)]ds. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Subtract the optimal average to get (6.16).

nodes.name: Estimate (6.17)
nodes.statement:
Note that if $A=0$, $B=\widehat{c}$, then (\ref{6.2}) and
(\ref{6.3}) imply $\overline{x}^N$ is bounded in
$L^2_{\mathcal{F}}(0,T;\mathbb{R}).$ Similarly, if (\ref{6.2}) and
(\ref{6.3}) hold with  $A=\widehat{f}$, $B=\widehat{c}$, then using
Lemma \ref{lemma6-1} to (\ref{6.16}), we have

\begin{eqnarray} &&\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt \nonumber\\ &&\leq
(1+K_2)\left[(36+12R^2)\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt+\frac{36}{N^{2}}L\cdot
\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}[u_{i}(s)-\widehat{u}_{i}(s)]^{2}ds\right],
\end{eqnarray}

where $L$ and $K_2$ are defined before.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3.2 yields estimate (6.17).

nodes.name: Restrict deviations
nodes.statement:
On the other hand, from Lemma \ref{lemma6.3},
$\mathcal{J}_i(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})$ is bounded, it then
suffices to consider $u_i$ in (\ref{6.13}) such that
$\mathcal{J}_i(u_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})\leq
\mathcal{J}_i(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})$, which implies that
$\mathbb{E}\int_0^T|u_i(t)|^2dt\leq C$.
nodes.statement_short: By Lemma 3.6 it suffices to consider bounded deviating controls.

nodes.name: Estimate (6.18)
nodes.statement_short: Bound the control difference (6.18).

nodes.name: Estimate (6.19)
nodes.statement:
Substituting (\ref{6.18}) into
(\ref{6.17}), we have

\begin{eqnarray} &&\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt\nonumber\\
&& \leq
(1+K_2)(36+12R^2)\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt\nonumber
\\
&&+\frac{C}{N^{2}}+ (1+K_2)\frac{72}{N^{2}R^2}L^2\cdot
\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}[u_{i}(s)-\widehat{u}_{i}(s)]^{2}ds.
\end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Combine into (6.19).

nodes.name: Estimate (6.20)
nodes.statement_short: Bound the deviating state (6.20).

nodes.name: Self-referential bound
nodes.statement_short: Substitute (6.19) into (6.20).

nodes.name: Absorption
nodes.statement:
So if $(1+K_2)K_1\frac{360}{N^{2}R^2}L^2<\frac 1 2,$ then we have
\[
\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)|^{2}dt\leq C+C\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{x}^{N}(t)-
\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt,
\]
which implies the boundedness of $\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)|^{2}dt$.
nodes.statement_short: Absorb the state term under the smallness condition.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: By combining (\ref{6.19}), (\ref{6.20}) and Lemma \ref{lemma-2}, we obtained the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude with Lemma 3.3.

nodes.name: Perturbation reformulation
nodes.statement:
If we denote by $\xi_a(t)=x^N(t)-\widehat{a}(t),$
$\xi_b(t)=\gamma(\widehat{a}(t)-x^N(t))$, then the dynamics and cost functional
of $\mathcal{A}_i$ can be rewritten as

\begin{align}
x_{i}(t) = & \; \varphi(t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)x_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds \nonumber \\
& +\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)\xi_{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma(t,s)dW_{i}(s), \end{align}

and

\[
J_{i}(u_{i})=\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{T}\left[ |x_{i}(t)-\gamma\widehat{a}(t)-\eta +\xi _{b}(t)|^{2}+R|u_{i}(t)|^{2}\right]dt.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Recast agent $i$'s problem as the perturbed problem with $\xi_a,\xi_b$.

nodes.name: Combine estimates
nodes.statement:
From Lemma \ref{lemma6.4}, we have
$\epsilon_a+\epsilon_b=O(\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}})$, and
$\mathbb{E}\int_0^T|x_i(t)|^2dt+\mathbb{E}\int_0^T|u_i(t)|^2dt\leq C,$ where $C$
is independent of $N$, $\epsilon_a$, $\epsilon_b$ are defined in
(\ref{6.6}), it then follows from Lemma \ref{lemma6.4}, Theorem
\ref{theorem3.2} that

\[
\mathcal{J}_i(u_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})\geq \overline{J}_i(\overline{u}_i)-O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}\right) \geq \mathcal{J}_i(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})-O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}\right).
\]

The conclusion is thus proved.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3.7 gives $\epsilon_a+\epsilon_b=O(1/\sqrt N)$; combine with Theorem 3.3.
